paper_title: Solar Cells Constructed with Polythiophene Thin Films Grown along Tethered Thiophene-Dye Conjugates via Photoelectrochemical Polymerization

knowledge_points.content: A polythiophene-based solar cell (PTSC) was constructed using photoelectrochemical polymerization of thiophene initiated by a sub-monolayer of 3-{5-[N,N-bis(4-diphenylamino)phenyl]thieno[3,2-b]thiophen-2-yl}-2-cyano-acrylic acid dye (C207) tethered to a compact TiO2 layer.
knowledge_points.evidence: A polythiophene-based solar cell (PTSC) is constructed by photoelectrochemically polymerizing thiophene onto an ultrathin compact TiO2 layer (150 nm thick) covered with a sub-monolayer of tethered 3-{5-[N,N-bis(4-diphenylamino)phenyl]thieno[3,2-b]thiophen-2-yl}-2-cyano-acrylic acid dye (ca. 10% coverage).

knowledge_points.content: The optimized PTSC featuring a 270 nm thick polythiophene film achieved a power conversion efficiency of 7.52 ± 0.58%, with a short-circuit current density (JSC) of 12.90 ± 0.63 mA/cm², an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 0.81 ± 0.01 V, and a fill factor (FF) of 0.72 ± 0.01.
knowledge_points.evidence: With a 270 nm thick PT film and 2,2',7,7'-tetrakis(N,N-di(4-methoxyphenyl)amino)-9,9'-spirobifluorene serving as the hole-transport material, the PTSC exhibited a short-circuit current density JSC of 12.90 ± 0.63 mA/cm², an open-circuit voltage VOC of 0.81 ± 0.01 V, and a fill factor of 0.72 ± 0.01. The high conversion efficiency (7.52 ± 0.58%) of the PTSC...

knowledge_points.content: The surface coverage of the C207 dye significantly impacts the polythiophene film morphology; an optimal coverage of approximately 10% (7.8 x 10^-11 mol/cm²) allows sufficient space for thiophene monomers to π-π stack onto the dye molecules, leading to ordered polymer growth.
knowledge_points.evidence: Formation of such a sub-monolayer of tethered dye molecules is key to the subsequent PT film grown, as space is provided for thiophene monomers to π-π stack onto the dye aromatic moieties... At coverages higher than 10%, the growth of PT film becomes accelerated, which leads to agglomeration of PT particles.

knowledge_points.content: Polythiophene film thickness affects device performance, with efficiency peaking at 270 nm; films thicker than this threshold exhibit rougher, more irregular morphologies and disordered structures that hinder charge transport and increase recombination.
knowledge_points.evidence: However, the PT film has a rougher morphology and contains larger and more irregular granules when its thickness exceeds 270 nm... the rougher morphology and disordered structure associated with PT films thicker than 270 nm... hinder the charge transport and cause more rapid hole/electron recombination.

knowledge_points.content: The use of cyclic voltammetry (cycling between -0.9 and 1.2 V) for photoelectrochemical polymerization results in a 28.28% higher conversion efficiency compared to constant potential deposition at 0.5 V, primarily due to the effective doping of the polythiophene film by cations from the electrolyte.
knowledge_points.evidence: The corresponding η is 5.4 ± 0.31%, a decrease of 28.28% when compared to that of the film prepared with cyclic voltammetry... This decrease is attributed to doping of the PT films by cations from the electrolyte solution.

knowledge_points.content: The PTSC architecture consists of an FTO substrate, a 150 nm compact TiO2 layer, a sub-monolayer of C207 dye, the polymerized polythiophene active layer, a Spiro-OMeTAD hole-transport layer, and a 90 nm gold (Au) anode.
knowledge_points.evidence: The dye/TiO2/FTO substrate was used as a working electrode... The hole-transport layer was spincoated onto the PT/dye/TiO2/FTO substrate using a chlorobenzene solution of 0.059 M spiro-OMeTAD... The anode assembly was completed by sputtering a 90 nm thick Au coating.

knowledge_points.content: Raman spectroscopy confirms the growth of polythiophene through the space between tethered dye molecules, as evidenced by the symmetric stretching of the thiophene ring at 1457 cm⁻¹ and the attenuation of dye-specific peaks between 1300 and 1700 cm⁻¹.
knowledge_points.evidence: The significant attenuation of these peaks in the red curve confirms the deposition of a PT film through the space between the tethered dye molecules... Upon PT film formation, the symmetric stretching of the thiophene ring within the polymer skeleton emerged at 1457 cm⁻¹.

knowledge_points.content: Electron lifetime (τn) measurements derived from open-circuit voltage decay curves indicate that the recombination process is charge-transfer controlled and that lifetimes decrease as the PT film thickness deviates from the optimal 270 nm due to increased disorder.
knowledge_points.evidence: The derivatives of the decay curves are an indirect way of measuring the electron lifetimes τn... The reverse logarithm linear dependence suggests that the recombination process is charge-transfer controlled... indicating that the hole/electron recombination increases as the PT film becomes rougher and less ordered.

knowledge_points.content: The photoelectrochemical polymerization of thiophene on the dye/TiO2/FTO substrate shows a significantly lower onset potential (-0.6 V vs Ag/AgCl) under irradiation compared to the dark condition (0.6 V vs Ag/AgCl).
knowledge_points.evidence: In the dark, the onset potential is about 0.6 V vs Ag/AgCl... In contrast, the onset potential decreases to -0.6 V under irradiation.

knowledge_points.content: The highly aligned polythiophene backbone grown via this method facilitates unidirectional charge transport, which is theoretically 10-fold greater along the backbone than perpendicular to it, thereby reducing recombination.
knowledge_points.evidence: Tremel et al. reported that the electron-transfer rate along the polymer backbone is 10-fold greater than that perpendicular to the backbone... Therefore, the PT backbone is an excellent one-dimensional nanostructure for electron transport and can delocalize charges while retarding the electron/hole recombination.
